macros.name: ekvcChange
macros.doc: This processes the ⟨key⟩=⟨value⟩ list for the macro ⟨cs⟩ to set new defaults for it (meaning the initial values used if you don’t provide anything at use time, not those specified with the default type).

macros.name: ekvcFlagGetHeight
macros.doc: This retrieves the current height of the ⟨flag⟩ and provides it as a braced argument to ⟨next⟩, leaving ⟨next⟩{⟨height⟩} in the input stream.

macros.name: ekvcFlagGetHeights
macros.doc: This retrieves the current height of each ⟨flag⟩ in the ⟨flag-list⟩ and provides them as a single argument to ⟨next⟩.

macros.name: ekvcFlagHeight
macros.doc: This expands to the current height of ⟨flag⟩ in a single step of expansion (without a trailing space).

macros.name: ekvcFlagIf
macros.doc: This interprets a ⟨flag⟩ as a boolean and expands to either ⟨true⟩ or ⟨false⟩.

macros.name: ekvcFlagIfRaised
macros.doc: This tests whether the ⟨flag⟩ is raised, meaning it has a height greater than zero, and if so expands to ⟨true⟩ else to ⟨false⟩.

macros.name: ekvcFlagNew
macros.doc: This initialises the macro ⟨flag⟩ as a new flag.

macros.name: ekvcFlagRaise
macros.doc: This expandably raises the height of ⟨flag⟩ by 1.

macros.name: ekvcFlagReset
macros.doc: This resets a flag (so restores its height to 0).

macros.name: ekvcFlagResetGlobal
macros.doc: This resets a flag (so restores its height to 0). This operation is not expandable and done locally for \ekvcFlagReset and globally for \ekvcFlagResetGlobal.

macros.name: ekvcHash
macros.doc: This defines ⟨cs⟩ to be a macro taking one mandatory argument which should contain a ⟨key⟩=⟨value⟩ list.

macros.name: ekvcHashAndForward
macros.doc: This defines ⟨cs⟩ to be a macro taking one mandatory argument which should contain a ⟨key⟩=⟨value⟩ list.

macros.name: ekvcPass
macros.doc: This passes ⟨value⟩ on to ⟨key⟩ for the expkv-cs-macro ⟨cs⟩.

macros.name: ekvcSecondaryKeys
macros.doc: This is the front facing macro to define secondary keys.

macros.name: ekvcSplit
macros.doc: This defines ⟨cs⟩ to be a macro taking one mandatory argument which should contain a ⟨key⟩=⟨value⟩ list.

macros.name: ekvcValue
macros.doc: This is a safe way to access your keys in a hash variant.

macros.name: ekvcValueFast
macros.doc: This behaves similar to \ekvcValue, but without any safefy tests.

macros.name: ekvcValueSplit
macros.doc: If you need a specific ⟨key⟩ from a ⟨key list⟩ more than once, it’ll be a good idea to only extract it once and from then on keep it as a separate argument (or if you want to forward this value to another macro). Hence the macro \ekvcValueSplit will extract one specific ⟨key⟩’s ⟨value⟩ from the list and forward it as an argument to ⟨next⟩, so the result of this will be ⟨next⟩{⟨value⟩}.

macros.name: ekvcValueSplitFast
macros.doc: This behaves just like \ekvcValueSplit, but it won’t run the safety tests, hence it is faster but more error prone, just like the relation between \ekvcValue and \ekvcValueFast.
